tier_rationale: T1 (folklore made precise: deallocating a frame before the tail call is known to be safe when no pointer into it reaches the callee (CompCert `Tailcall.v` documentation, LLVM `musttail` documentation), and tail calls without destructors are mechanized in Stack-Aware CompCert and CakeML; a mechanized statement combining pre-jump destructor finalization with this equivalence was not found in a web search)
plain_claim: For every toy program `p` satisfying `NoStackBorrow p` (in the unbounded `preJump` run of `p`, no executed `tailCall` passes an argument value that is a pointer into the current frame), and for every outcome `o` and event trace `es`, the unbounded `frameReuse` run of `p` halts with `o` and `es` if and only if the unbounded `preJump` run of `p` does.

hypotheses.name: hnb : NoStackBorrow p
hypotheses.purpose: frame reuse removes the current frame before the callee runs; a callee loading through a pointer into it is `ub` under `frameReuse` but reads a live slot under `preJump`
hypotheses.witness_class: a three-function program with one tail call passing `addrOf` of a local

nonvacuity_witness: `dtorProg` satisfies `NoStackBorrow` and both semantics return 0 with trace `[drop 7, out 1]`.
non_claims: Compares halted runs (outcome and finite trace). Infinite traces of non-halting runs are not compared, beyond the consequence of the equivalence that one run halts exactly when the other does.
Unbounded stack (`D = none`). Under a bound the two semantics differ (`frameReuse_of_preJump_fails_for_overflow_countUp3`); the bounded transfer is card R3.
Does not relate `frameReuse` to `callReturn`: they differ even under the hypothesis (card R2).

`NoStackBorrow` is sufficient, not necessary: in `ignorePtrProg` a pointer into the current frame is passed but never loaded through, so `NoStackBorrow` fails, yet the two semantics have the same outcomes and traces (`noStackBorrow_not_necessary_ignorePtrProg`).
`NoStackBorrow` is a dynamic property of the unbounded `preJump` run; it is not a static check. A sound static check is card R8.

`preJump` keeps finalized frames on the stack, and the machine does not flag a load from a dropped slot (`Frame.kill` clears the drop flag and keeps the value); it imposes no arity or signature relation between a function and the callee of its tail call (a mismatch is `ub` at `push`).

Destructors are atomic events (`DtorKind`): running one pushes no frame, executes no instruction and reads or writes no slot, so destructors that call functions (raising the peak depth during finalization) or that access their own slot through `&mut self` are not modelled (the `popFirst` variant of card R19 models that access and nothing else).
The toy has no heap, no stores through pointers, no borrow checker and no catching of panics.
Frame identities are unobservable by construction: `Val.obs` maps pointers and `undef` to `0`, and events and final results record `Val.obs` values and no frame identities.
Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc or any other compiler.

hypotheses.purpose: the verdict whose soundness is claimed

`taint` runs `nSlots + 1` rounds of an inflationary step; the proof shows that the result is a fixpoint of `taintStep` (in the proof-support module `EscapeProof.lean`, not cited as a result); that it is the least fixpoint is not proved, and the result is about `taint` as defined.

plain_claim: For every state `st` about to execute `tailCall f args` under `frameReuse` (any bound `D`) — not unwinding, with no pending return, and with the arguments evaluating without `ub` to evaluated frame `fr1` — if exactly one pending destructor of `fr1` panics, the step still emits one `drop` per slot pending in `fr1` (slots moved into the arguments are no longer pending), in `pendingDrops` order, removes the frame, and continues unwinding with the frames below (`unwindBelow`: the original caller's cleanup, or outcome `panicked` if there is none); the already-evaluated argument values are discarded without a `drop` event.

tier_rationale: T1 (folklore made precise: LLVM documents that the callee popping the argument area makes mandatory tail calls possible and that `musttail` under `swifttailcc`/`tailcc` does not require matching prototypes; a statement relating cleanup convention, boundary relocation and argument areas was not found mechanized)
plain_claim: In the layout toy with the boundary moved by `δ` cells before the jump (callee area at `[b + δ - inH, b + δ)`), for all `δ`, `inG` and `inH`: `δ = 0` gives exactly the fixed-boundary `ReuseSound`; under callee cleanup frame reuse is sound iff `δ = inH - inG` (integer subtraction), so a suitable relocation exists for all area sizes; under caller cleanup it is sound iff `δ = 0` and `inH ≤ inG`, so relocation does not help.
nonvacuity_witness: Under callee cleanup, `inG = 1`, `inH = 2`: unsound at the fixed boundary, sound with `δ = 1`; under caller cleanup, `δ = 0`, `inG = 2`, `inH = 1`.
non_claims: Writing the relocated return address, and the cost of the extra moves, are not modelled.
The second condition holds for all sizes and relocations (`readArgs_reuseWriteAt`); overlapping in-place argument copies are not modelled.

Says nothing about which convention rustc or LLVM uses for a given ABI; the LLVM and rustc texts of the modeling bridge (Findings) are quoted as documentation and source text (including test files), not as execution evidence establishing which calling convention either compiler lowers a given ABI to.
Register-passed arguments, per-argument types and alignment are not modelled.

The third condition is fixed by `spAfterReturnAt`, which stipulates each convention's stack pointer after the return; under callee cleanup the `→` direction of `reuseSoundAt_calleePops_iff` follows from it alone, and under caller cleanup so does `δ = 0`.
A separate layout model; no relation to the frame-stack machine is proved.
Addresses and `δ` are integers (no wrap-around, no truncated subtraction); area sizes 0 are allowed and covered.
Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc or any other compiler.
